Launch HN: HyperProbe (YC S26) – Agents that do read-only debugging in prod (hyperprobe.co)
64 points by shailendraht 18 hours ago | hide | past | favorite | 45 comments

Hi HN, this is Shailendra and Karan here. We are building a fast and safe way for coding agents to debug issues live in production.

When prod breaks, it lets Cursor, Claude, and others drop virtual breakpoints or probes safely in your running code, and extract the exact variable values that logs don’t have.

All this saves time and effort for engineers who’d otherwise dig through logs and traces or redeploy with console.logs or print statements until they find the root cause.

Here is the link to the video that explains this: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ivV7I--ta5c

Agents write most of our code now. This shrinks the useful context engineers need to debug AI written code, a problem not helped by the limited telemetry added in the same code by AI.

So when something breaks in prod, the first instinct for an engineer is to open logs or throw them to your agents. But if the line you are looking for is not there, agents will start guessing the root cause on non-existent data, forcing you to add a log, and redeploy.

This analysis-inference loop of agents with existing data does not come cheap, burning a lot of tokens. And the add log, redeploy cycle is so slow and painful that it makes engineers hate on-call.

Our approach lets agents capture telemetry on-demand at the exact moment and point of failure, killing the log-redeploy cycle and getting the most accurate RCA while burning fewer tokens.

The obvious problem is making it work on a running service. You can't pause a live service the way you'd pause a debugger on your laptop. Getting the value out of a running process safely, without pausing a thread or slowing the host is the challenge.We are making this happen.

Before this I ran engineering at a 100 member team. Then Karan and I spent three years on HyperTest which was a testing tool.

At HyperTest, we turned production traffic into integration tests using OpenTelemetry. That was production instrumentation too. The hard parts of pulling real runtime state out of a running service without breaking it, were the hard parts we learnt to put together.

We learnt some other lessons the hard way too. HyperTest tried to prevent bugs with better tests, and adoption was a fight every time. Calls kept getting cancelled because teams were firefighting production. Testing was hygiene. Broken prod was hair on fire. This made us see where priorities lie.

This seeded the idea of building a truly autonomous on-call agent i.e. one that takes an alert, probes, diagnoses and fixes it in a few minutes. But this is how it works as of now:

You talk to your coding agent the way you already do. Tell it what's wrong: "checkout returns 200 but some users are seeing their order fail, find out why." It locates the line in your local code, connects to us over MCP, and drops a probe on that line in the running service. The probe is read-only and sits dormant until real traffic hits. When hit, it captures the local variables at every frame of the call stack at that exact moment. It hands them to the agent, which diagnoses with real data.

There are two pieces. An SDK that runs inside your service, and an MCP server your coding agent talks to. The SDK is what makes setting probes (virtual breakpoints, log or metric) possible without a redeploy. In Node and Python it hooks in-process. In Java it attaches as a JVM agent, instrumenting at the bytecode level. Either way the service keeps running and serving traffic. Nothing pauses.

When your agent wants to look at a line, it calls the MCP server, which tells the SDK to place a probe there. When a request hits the line, the SDK captures what the probe asked for, sanitizes it in-process, and streams it back to the agent via the MCP.

This can run inside prod, so a probe can read any value sitting in that variable. We ensure redaction happens in-process, inside your own container's memory. This is before anything goes on the wire. Keys like password, token, authorization, ssn and credit card are redacted by default and you add your own.

Also the probes read but never write, and if you want no captured state to ever leave your network you can self host the server, broker, and even the database in your infra.

On overhead: when idle, the SDK adds negligible memory and effectively nothing to throughput and response time. Probes only cost anything while actively capturing. Also captures are bounded. A separate monitor watches in real time and pulls every active probe if overhead ever spikes.

Every log-and-trace tool hands the agent data that already exists and asks it to reason backward to what probably happened. We think it is more useful to give agents eyes and ears into the running code, so they capture what they need when they need it, right at the point of failure.

This seems like the simplest and fastest way to debug prod incidents.

We’d love the community to try this in any environment to debug any known or unknown issue by just chatting with your coding agent. And let us know what more features you need to make this a truly autonomous on-call agent

Supported platforms: NodeJs, Java, Python.

The obvious problem is making it work on a running service. You can't pause a live service the way you'd pause a debugger on your laptop. Getting the value out of a running process safely, without pausing a thread or slowing the host is the challenge.We are making this happen.

Before this I ran engineering at a 100 member team. Then Karan and I spent three years on HyperTest which was a testing tool.

At HyperTest, we turned production traffic into integration tests using OpenTelemetry. That was production instrumentation too. The hard parts of pulling real runtime state out of a running service without breaking it, were the hard parts we learnt to put together.

We learnt some other lessons the hard way too. HyperTest tried to prevent bugs with better tests, and adoption was a fight every time. Calls kept getting cancelled because teams were firefighting production. Testing was hygiene. Broken prod was hair on fire. This made us see where priorities lie.

This seeded the idea of building a truly autonomous on-call agent i.e. one that takes an alert, probes, diagnoses and fixes it in a few minutes. But this is how it works as of now:

You talk to your coding agent the way you already do. Tell it what's wrong: "checkout returns 200 but some users are seeing their order fail, find out why." It locates the line in your local code, connects to us over MCP, and drops a probe on that line in the running service. The probe is read-only and sits dormant until real traffic hits. When hit, it captures the local variables at every frame of the call stack at that exact moment. It hands them to the agent, which diagnoses with real data.

There are two pieces. An SDK that runs inside your service, and an MCP server your coding agent talks to. The SDK is what makes setting probes (virtual breakpoints, log or metric) possible without a redeploy. In Node and Python it hooks in-process. In Java it attaches as a JVM agent, instrumenting at the bytecode level. Either way the service keeps running and serving traffic. Nothing pauses.

When your agent wants to look at a line, it calls the MCP server, which tells the SDK to place a probe there. When a request hits the line, the SDK captures what the probe asked for, sanitizes it in-process, and streams it back to the agent via the MCP.

This can run inside prod, so a probe can read any value sitting in that variable. We ensure redaction happens in-process, inside your own container's memory. This is before anything goes on the wire. Keys like password, token, authorization, ssn and credit card are redacted by default and you add your own.

Also the probes read but never write, and if you want no captured state to ever leave your network you can self host the server, broker, and even the database in your infra.

On overhead: when idle, the SDK adds negligible memory and effectively nothing to throughput and response time. Probes only cost anything while actively capturing. Also captures are bounded. A separate monitor watches in real time and pulls every active probe if overhead ever spikes.

Every log-and-trace tool hands the agent data that already exists and asks it to reason backward to what probably happened. We think it is more useful to give agents eyes and ears into the running code, so they capture what they need when they need it, right at the point of failure.

This seems like the simplest and fastest way to debug prod incidents.

We’d love the community to try this in any environment to debug any known or unknown issue by just chatting with your coding agent. And let us know what more features you need to make this a truly autonomous on-call agent

Supported platforms: NodeJs, Java, Python.

sentences.zh: SDK 使得无需重新部署即可设置探针（虚拟断点、日志或指标）。

sentences.en: In Node and Python it hooks in-process.
sentences.zh: 在 Node 和 Python 中，它在进程内挂钩。

sentences.en: In Java it attaches as a JVM agent, instrumenting at the bytecode level.
sentences.zh: 在 Java 中，它作为 JVM 代理附加，在字节码级别进行检测。

sentences.en: Either way the service keeps running and serving traffic.
sentences.zh: 无论哪种方式，服务都会保持运行并提供流量。

sentences.en: Nothing pauses.
sentences.zh: 一切都没有暂停。

blocks.html_en: When your agent wants to look at a line, it calls the MCP server, which tells the SDK to place a probe there. When a request hits the line, the SDK captures what the probe asked for, sanitizes it in-process, and streams it back to the agent via the MCP.

sentences.en: When your agent wants to look at a line, it calls the MCP server, which tells the SDK to place a probe there.
sentences.zh: 当您的代理想要查看线路时，它会调用 MCP 服务器，该服务器告诉 SDK 在那里放置探测器。

sentences.en: When a request hits the line, the SDK captures what the probe asked for, sanitizes it in-process, and streams it back to the agent via the MCP.
sentences.zh: 当请求到达线路时，SDK 会捕获探测器请求的内容，在进程中对其进行清理，然后通过 MCP 将其流回代理。

blocks.html_en: This can run inside prod, so a probe can read any value sitting in that variable. We ensure redaction happens in-process, inside your own container's memory. This is before anything goes on the wire. Keys like password, token, authorization, ssn and credit card are redacted by default and you add your own.

sentences.en: This can run inside prod, so a probe can read any value sitting in that variable.
sentences.zh: 这可以在产品内部运行，因此探针可以读取该变量中的任何值。

sentences.en: We ensure redaction happens in-process, inside your own container's memory.
sentences.zh: 我们确保编辑在您自己的容器内存中进行。

sentences.en: This is before anything goes on the wire.
sentences.zh: 这是在任何事情发生之前。

sentences.en: Keys like password, token, authorization, ssn and credit card are redacted by default and you add your own.
sentences.zh: 密码、令牌、授权、ssn 和信用卡等密钥默认经过编辑，您可以添加自己的密钥。

blocks.html_en: Also the probes read but never write, and if you want no captured state to ever leave your network you can self host the server, broker, and even the database in your infra.

sentences.en: Also the probes read but never write, and if you want no captured state to ever leave your network you can self host the server, broker, and even the database in your infra.
sentences.zh: 此外，探针读取但从不写入，如果您不希望捕获的状态离开您的网络，您可以在您的基础设施中自行托管服务器、代理，甚至数据库。

blocks.html_en: On overhead: when idle, the SDK adds negligible memory and effectively nothing to throughput and response time. Probes only cost anything while actively capturing. Also captures are bounded. A separate monitor watches in real time and pulls every active probe if overhead ever spikes.

sentences.en: On overhead: when idle, the SDK adds negligible memory and effectively nothing to throughput and response time.
sentences.zh: 关于开销：空闲时，SDK 增加的内存可以忽略不计，并且实际上不会增加​​吞吐量和响应时间。

sentences.en: Probes only cost anything while actively capturing.
sentences.zh: 探测器在主动捕获时只需要花费任何费用。

sentences.en: Also captures are bounded.
sentences.zh: 捕获也是有限的。

sentences.en: A separate monitor watches in real time and pulls every active probe if overhead ever spikes.
sentences.zh: 一个单独的监视器实时监视并在开销出现峰值时拉动每个活动探头。

blocks.html_en: Every log-and-trace tool hands the agent data that already exists and asks it to reason backward to what probably happened. We think it is more useful to give agents eyes and ears into the running code, so they capture what they need when they need it, right at the point of failure.

sentences.en: Every log-and-trace tool hands the agent data that already exists and asks it to reason backward to what probably happened.
sentences.zh: 每个日志和跟踪工具都会处理已经存在的代理数据，并要求其向后推理可能发生的情况。

sentences.en: We think it is more useful to give agents eyes and ears into the running code, so they capture what they need when they need it, right at the point of failure.
sentences.zh: 我们认为让代理了解正在运行的代码更有用，这样他们就可以在需要时、在发生故障时捕获所需的内容。

blocks.html_en: This seems like the simplest and fastest way to debug prod incidents.

sentences.en: This seems like the simplest and fastest way to debug prod incidents.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是调试产品事件最简单、最快的方法。

blocks.html_en: We’d love the community to try this in any environment to debug any known or unknown issue by just chatting with your coding agent. And let us know what more features you need to make this a truly autonomous on-call agent

sentences.en: We’d love the community to try this in any environment to debug any known or unknown issue by just chatting with your coding agent.
sentences.zh: 我们希望社区能够在任何环境中尝试此操作，只需与您的编码代理聊天即可调试任何已知或未知的问题。

sentences.en: And let us know what more features you need to make this a truly autonomous on-call agent
sentences.zh: 让我们知道您还需要哪些功能才能使其成为真正的自主待命代理

blocks.html_en: Supported platforms: NodeJs, Java, Python.

sentences.en: Supported platforms: NodeJs, Java, Python.
sentences.zh: 支持的平台：NodeJs、Java、Python。

content_html_zh: 启动 HN：HyperProbe (YC S26) – 在 prod 中进行只读调试的代理 (hyperprobe.co)64 分，作者：shailendraht 18 小时前 |隐藏 |过去|最喜欢 | 45 条评论嗨 HN，我是 Shailendra 和 Karan。 我们正在为编码代理构建一种快速、安全的方法来调试生产中的问题。当产品出现故障时，它可以让 Cursor、Claude 和其他人在运行的代码中安全地删除虚拟断点或探针，并提取日志中没有的确切变量值。所有这些都为工程师节省了时间和精力，否则他们会挖掘日志和跟踪或使用 console.logs 或打印语句重新部署，直到找到根本原因。以下是解释此问题的视频链接： https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ivV7I--ta5cAgents 现在编写我们的大部分代码。 这缩小了工程师调试人工智能编写的代码所需的有用上下文，而人工智能在同一代码中添加的有限遥测技术并不能解决这个问题。因此，当产品出现问题时，工程师的第一反应是打开日志或将它们扔给您的代理。 但是，如果您要查找的行不存在，代理将开始猜测不存在数据的根本原因，迫使您添加日志并重新部署。这种使用现有数据对代理进行分析推理循环并不便宜，会消耗大量代币。 添加日志、重新部署周期是如此缓慢和痛苦，以至于工程师讨厌随叫随到。我们的方法让代理在准确的时刻和故障点按需捕获遥测数据，消除日志重新部署周期并获得最准确的 RCA，同时消耗更少的代币。明显的问题是让它在正在运行的服务上工作。 您无法像暂停笔记本电脑上的调试器一样暂停实时服务。 安全地从正在运行的进程中获取价值，而不暂停线程或减慢主机速度是一项挑战。我们正在实现这一目标。在此之前，我在一个 100 名成员的团队中负责工程工作。 然后我和 Karan 花了三年时间研究 HyperTest，这是一个测试工具。在 HyperTest，我们使用 OpenTelemetry 将生产流量转化为集成测试。 那也是生产仪器。 从正在运行的服务中提取真实的运行时状态而不破坏它的困难部分，是我们学会将其组合在一起的困难部分。我们还通过艰难的方式学到了其他一些教训。 HyperTest 试图通过更好的测试来防止错误，但每次采用都是一场斗争。 由于团队正在进行消防生产，电话不断被取消。 测试是卫生的。 折断的刺棒使头发着火。 这让我们看到了优先事项在哪里。这萌生了构建一个真正自主的待命代理的想法，即一个可以在几分钟内接收警报、探测、诊断并修复它的代理。 但这就是它现在的工作方式：你按照你已经做的方式与你的编码代理交谈。 告诉它出了什么问题：“结账返回 200，但有些用户发现他们的订单失败，找出原因。” 它会在本地代码中找到该行，通过 MCP 连接到我们，并在正在运行的服务中对该行进行探测。 该探测器是只读的，并处于休眠状态，直到真正的流量到来为止。 当命中时，它会捕获当时调用堆栈的每一帧的局部变量。 它将它们交给代理，代理使用真实数据进行诊断。有两部分。 在您的服务内运行的 SDK，以及与您的编码代理通信的 MCP 服务器。 SDK 使得无需重新部署即可设置探针（虚拟断点、日志或指标）。 在 Node 和 Python 中，它在进程内挂钩。 在 Java 中，它作为 JVM 代理附加，在字节码级别进行检测。 无论哪种方式，服务都会保持运行并提供流量。 没有任何暂停。当您的代理想要查看线路时，它会调用 MCP 服务器，该服务器告诉 SDK 在那里放置探测器。 当请求到达线路时，SDK 会捕获探针请求的内容，在进程中对其进行清理，并通过 MCP 将其流回代理。这可以在产品内部运行，因此探针可以读取该变量中的任何值。 我们确保编辑在您自己的容器内存中进行。 这是在任何事情发生之前。 密码、令牌、授权、ssn 和信用卡等密钥默认情况下会被编辑，您可以添加自己的密钥。此外，探针会读取但从不写入，如果您不希望捕获的状态离开您的网络，您可以在基础设施中自行托管服务器、代理，甚至数据库。开销方面：闲置时，SDK 会添加可忽略不计的内存，并且实际上不会增加​​吞吐量和响应时间。 探测器在主动捕获时只需要花费任何费用。 捕获也是有限的。 一个单独的监视器实时监视，并在开销出现峰值时拉动每个活动探测器。每个日志和跟踪工具都会处理已经存在的代理数据，并要求其向后推理可能发生的情况。 我们认为，让代理能够密切关注正在运行的代码，这样他们就可以在需要时捕获所需的内容，就在故障点。这似乎是调试产品事件的最简单、最快的方法。我们希望社区能够在任何环境中尝试此方法，只需与编码代理聊天即可调试任何已知或未知的问题。 让我们知道您还需要哪些功能才能使其成为真正的自主待命代理支持的平台：NodeJs、Java、Python。 帮助
